text: ADR-001 selects FalkorDB v4.18.1 as the storage backend for Graphiti, replacing the upstream default of Neo4j. The choice is driven by FalkorDB's lower memory footprint on the homelab's modest hardware and its Redis-compatible protocol on port 6379. Operators run it as a Docker container bound to 127.0.0.1 with persistence enabled via AOF rewrite plus periodic RDB snapshots.

ADR-002 adopts gpt-4o-mini as the Phase 1 extraction LLM for Graphiti. At roughly $0.30 per month for 500 episodes, it stays well under the $20 monthly budget cap defined in NFR-COST-001. The Graphiti maintainers explicitly warn that smaller local models produce malformed JSON that breaks ingestion, so a stable cloud model is preferred until a validation gate confirms a local alternative.

ADR-003 keeps text-embedding-3-small on OpenAI's API regardless of where the extraction LLM runs. Embeddings remain on cloud because no local equivalent matches its quality at the cost point, and the embedding API is independently reliable from chat completion endpoints. This decision is unchanged by Phase 4 LiteLLM bridging.

ADR-004 selects GitNexus over Graphify and CodeGraphContext for the code-graph layer. GitNexus is already operational in the homelab, integrates with the Claude Code MCP surface, and avoids the speculative 71x token-reduction claim that Graphify's marketing makes but real-world usage shows closer to 5-10x.

ADR-005 chooses an MCP-first integration approach over a skill-first one. MCP servers expose tools that survive across Claude Code sessions and can be invoked by sub-agents, while skills are local to the operator's workspace and cannot be triggered by automation. For the Context Stack, MCP is the durable surface.

ADR-006 represents the wiki as a flat file tree of markdown files inside homelab-playbook. The decision rejects a database-backed wiki because the operator already has git for versioning, the search surface is just ripgrep, and any future migration is a `find ... -name '*.md'` away from being parseable by another tool.

ADR-007 specifies the Graphiti backup strategy: a nightly cron job runs `BGREWRITEAOF` against FalkorDB to compact the AOF, then takes an RDB snapshot, then ships both to a remote restic repository. A monthly Cypher export complements the binary backups for human-auditable disaster recovery.

ADR-008 implements a daily $1 hard cap on combined OpenAI spend across extraction and embedding. The cap is enforced by a polling check against the OpenAI usage API; on cap-exceeded, Graphiti's writes are rejected at the MCP boundary with a clear operator-facing error rather than silently failing.

ADR-009 defines the wiki-query skill as a thin ripgrep-plus-formatting wrapper. The skill is invoked by the user with a phrase like 'check the wiki for X' and returns a structured result: top-3 matching headings, file paths, and a 3-line snippet from each match. No LLM is involved in the lookup itself.

ADR-010 mandates that the decommission of MemPalace and OMEGA happens as a single pull request rather than an incremental migration. The single-PR shape forces the operator to verify all callers have been re-pointed before the merge, eliminating the half-state where two memory systems coexist and drift.

ADR-011 documents the Phase 4 LiteLLM bridge: route Graphiti's extraction calls to the operator's hybrid-gemma stack via OPENAI_BASE_URL, with no fork of the Graphiti MCP server. The bridge is gated on a 95% well-formed-JSON validation gate and is reversible by reverting a single environment variable.

ADR-012 specifies that GitNexus's graph export wrapper outputs a Cypher dump format rather than a proprietary GitNexus binary. The export is compatible with FalkorDB's `redis-cli --cluster import` path and with Neo4j's `cypher-shell --file` path, keeping the export human-auditable and the migration path open.

ADR-013 defines the tier-of-truth division across the Context Stack. Tier 1 is the wiki — durable, version-controlled, human-curated. Tier 2 is Graphiti — temporal, decision-tracking, machine-extracted. Tier 3 is GitNexus — code-graph, reset-on-rebuild, derived from source. Conflicts resolve to the lowest tier with the freshest commit date.

ADR-014 recalibrates the MoSCoW distribution from 86% MUST to roughly 60% MUST. Sixteen functional requirements move from MUST to SHOULD and three move from MUST to COULD. Decommission completeness and rollback FRs are deliberately excluded from downgrade because their absence would leave the migration unsafe.

An architectural decision was made to keep the Graphiti backup retention at 30 days rather than the upstream default of 7 days. The operator's homelab has ample storage on the hdd-pool, and the longer window covers the time it typically takes to notice a corrupted episode and trace it back to a specific ingest event.

On 2026-04-25, the operator decided to use cloud gpt-4o-mini for Phase 1 Graphiti extraction. On 2026-04-26, that decision was superseded by an empirical spike result authorising local Gemma 4 26B-MoE for Sprint 3, conditional on a 95% well-formed-JSON gate. The cloud fallback path remains available.

On 2026-04-23, pve1 began crashing on a roughly 16-hour cycle following its LVM-to-ZFS migration. On 2026-04-24, soft_panic and panic_on_oops kernel parameters were armed to capture a stack trace on the next crash. The original migration decision from 2026-04-15 is still considered correct, but the post-migration stability assumption is now open.

On 2026-04-11, the AI dev container architecture was approved with a layered config and dual-model design. On 2026-04-18, Epic 2 completed and Epic 3 was cued up. The original three-epic scope was unchanged, but the test-container-before-production policy was added on 2026-04-20 in response to lessons from Sprint 1.

On 2026-04-15, OMEGA was the active long-term memory system. On 2026-04-25, Context Stack Sprint 1 began the work to replace OMEGA and MemPalace with Graphiti plus a Tier 1 wiki. By Sprint 5 (week 10), OMEGA will be fully decommissioned and removed from CLAUDE.md.

On 2026-04-25, the hybrid-gemma serving stack reached MVP with 17 of 17 stories shipped. On 2026-04-26, that stack was selected as the candidate LLM bridge for Graphiti, conditional on the 50-fact validation spike. The earlier ADR-002 cloud-only Phase 1 decision is amended pending the spike result.

On 2026-04-18, ct-quant-trading was created on pve3 with VMID 162 and IP 192.168.50.162. On 2026-04-22, the container was migrated to local-zfs storage. The original 4C/8GB/50GB sizing is unchanged, but the storage tier moved from local-lvm to local-zfs to match the new pve3 storage layout.

On 2026-04-24, pve2 completed Window B of its ZFS migration and rejoined the cluster. CT151 was migrated back to pve2 on the same day. The pre-migration state where CT151 lived on pve1 is now invalid; pve2 is the authoritative home for ct-sparkle-cps as of 2026-04-24.

On 2026-04-25, the Graphiti backup retention policy was set to 30 days. On 2026-04-26, that policy is unchanged but a monthly Cypher export was added on top, with the first export scheduled for the end of May 2026. Both the binary and the Cypher exports ship to the same restic repository.

On 2026-04-25, ADR-002 specified gpt-4o-mini as the Phase 1 extraction model. On 2026-04-26, ADR-017 was authored to record the empirical validation of Gemma 4 26B-MoE as a candidate replacement. ADR-002 itself is amended only if the spike passes the 95% gate.

On 2026-04-26, the operator chose Pattern E-Azure over Pattern E-Oracle for cloud disaster recovery. The earlier multi-vendor research from 2026-04-25 was preserved but its recommendation reversed because the operator preferred adding to an existing Azure tenant rather than onboarding Oracle for a sub-10-euro-per-month delta.

The YAML block-scalar trap from Sprint 2: `>-` and `|-` keep `\s` literal, which silently breaks any regex pattern stored in those scalars. The lesson is to use inline double-quoted strings for regex values in Ansible, never block-scalars. This was discovered when an Ansible-templated alert rule failed to fire and the issue was traced to the regex never matching.

PVE 9.x replaced ha-manager groupadd with `ha-manager rules add node-affinity`, and resources are required at creation time rather than added later. The Sprint 1 retro flagged this when the original migration runbook used the deprecated command and silently produced an empty group. The runbook was updated and the lesson stored as feedback_pve9_ha_rules_migration.

Always audit replication before running pull-plug HA drills. The drills 6 and 7 caught a misconfiguration on ct:151 where ha-manager rules pointed at pve1+pve2 but /etc/pve/replication.cfg only replicated to pve3. HA without replication equals failover failure. The runbook now requires cross-checking both files before any failover test.

After stopping cron during PVE maintenance, always restart cron before closing the maintenance window. pve2 was left with cron stopped for 22 hours after Window B, and all textfile exporters silently went stale. Prometheus continued scraping but the metrics were 22 hours old. The lesson is now in feedback_pve_maintenance_cron.

Tailscale auth keys expire every 90 days, and a container will report healthy while logged out. The fix is to regenerate the auth key and recreate the compose stack. Healthchecks should be extended to include `tailscale status | grep -q 'tailnet'` to surface this state. Stored as feedback_tailscale_auth_recovery.

PVE 9 ha-manager rejects `set --state stopped` on resources that are in error state. The recovery sequence is disabled, then diagnose, then started. In some cases the resource config must be moved between /etc/pve/nodes/*/lxc/ directories manually before ha-manager will accept the new state. Lesson stored as feedback_pve9_ha_error_recovery.

Browser validation via Playwright catches issues that pure API checks miss. A Sprint 2 deploy passed all curl-based smoke tests but the actual UI rendered an error banner due to a CORS misconfiguration. The lesson is to add Playwright MCP to the post-deploy checklist for any user-facing service.

Sprint retros surfaced that BMad epic gates should run at sprint planning entry and at sprint retro exit, not just per-story. The story-level Task 0 was useful but did not catch cross-story integration risk. The new gate cadence is Entry Gate at planning, Exit Gate at retro, with explicit go/no-go for the next sprint.

When fixing a bug, follow the existing pattern exactly rather than introducing a quick workaround. A Sprint 2 fix added a try/except around a known-flaky API call, which masked a deeper retry-budget bug. The lesson is feedback_correct_fix: always trace the root cause and fix at the lowest layer that owns the invariant.

Phone notifications via ntfy must use the Tailscale tailnet hostname, not public DNS. The Android ntfy app cannot reach CT101 over public DNS because no public A record exists, but it can reach the tailnet hostname over the Tailscale tunnel. The Tailscale-only default is now baseline for all phone-facing services.

OMEGA depends on a SQLite-backed memory store. OMEGA is being replaced by Graphiti for temporal facts and by a markdown wiki for durable lessons. SQLite remains a dependency only for legacy read-back during the decommission window. After Sprint 5, the SQLite file is archived and OMEGA is removed.

MemPalace depends on a custom Python service running in CT101. MemPalace is being replaced by the same Graphiti+wiki pair that replaces OMEGA. The CT101 service is left running but unbound from CLAUDE.md as of Sprint 4, then decommissioned and the container destroyed at end of Sprint 5.

ct-sparkle-cps was originally hosted on pve1 and depended on local-lvm storage. It was migrated to pve2 on 2026-04-24, which now uses a ZFS mirror. Local-lvm on pve1 is no longer authoritative for CT151; the new authoritative storage is rpool/data on pve2.

The hybrid-gemma stack originally planned to use the Unsloth UD-Q5_K_M reasoner. During Sprint 1 of Epic 9, the operator overrode that choice in favour of the TrevorJS Q4_K_M build because the gate test passed at the bare upstream. The Unsloth choice is now superseded by TrevorJS, with Unsloth held in reserve for Sprint 4 Story 9.22.

The original AI dev container plan deployed straight to ct-dev-homelab. After Sprint 1 lessons, the deployment path now requires a stop in ct-dev-test (192.168.50.152) per story before promotion to ct-dev-homelab. The single-stage path is superseded by the two-stage test-then-prod pipeline.

Storage monitoring originally used hand-edited Prometheus targets in /etc/prometheus/. That approach is superseded by Terraform-driven file_sd_configs that auto-discover storage targets, with the Storage Overview Grafana dashboard rendering the result. The hand-edited path is decommissioned as of Sprint 3 of the storage-monitoring epic.

PVE3's storage layout originally used a single-pool ZFS configuration. The redesign moves it to a 2-way rpool plus a special vdev plus a fast-pool target, with media (354GB) preserved via zfs send. pve1 and pve2 require an LVM-to-ZFS conversion to match the redesign; pve2 is done as of 2026-04-24, pve1 is in flight.

The graphify pilot was originally scheduled as a homelab-playbook 4-week trial starting 2026-04-25. The pilot was downgraded to adopt-with-caveats after the research showed real-world token reduction was 5-10x rather than the marketed 71.5x. GitNexus took graphify's slot in ADR-004.

Originally, the Context Stack plan had three sprints. After PRD review, the plan expanded to five sprints over ten weeks to accommodate decommission completeness FRs and the Phase 4 LiteLLM bridge stretch. The three-sprint plan is superseded by the five-sprint plan, captured in the project memory as project_context_stack.

Cloud DR research originally compared Pattern A through E across Oracle, Azure, AWS, and Hetzner. Pattern E-Oracle was the best on raw price, but it was superseded by Pattern E-Azure once the operator's preference for single-vendor consolidation on the existing Azure tenant was factored in. Epic 7 now reflects the Azure choice.

On 2026-04-25, Tom deployed Graphiti MCP v1.0.2 onto ct-dev-homelab (192.168.50.151) using FalkorDB v4.18.1 as the backend. The container is fronted by Claude Code's MCP surface and reaches FalkorDB over 127.0.0.1:6379. The first ingest used gpt-4o-mini for extraction and text-embedding-3-small for embeddings, both via the OpenAI API.

Tom restarted llama-server-26b on ct-ai-01 (192.168.50.160) on 2026-04-25 to load the TrevorJS Q4_K_M build. LiteLLM gateway on port 4000 now exposes gemma4-26b-text, gemma4-e4b-vision, and gemma4-auto. Open WebUI on port 3000 routes through LiteLLM with bearer auth. Prometheus on host 192.168.50.165 scrapes /metrics every 15 seconds.

On 2026-04-24, ct-sparkle-cps (VMID 151) returned to pve2 (192.168.50.102) after Window B closed. The container hosts six CPS-Fabric repos with vault-encrypted Azure DevOps credentials. Tom verified the migration by SSHing in as root and running `git status` in /opt/cps-fabric/, which showed the working tree clean against the origin remote.

ct-quant-trading (VMID 162) lives on pve3 with IP 192.168.50.162 since 2026-04-18. The container runs Debian 13 on local-zfs with 4 cores, 8 GB RAM, and 50 GB disk. Tom uses it for quant-trading research, primarily Python notebooks against historical market data. The container has no public exposure and is reachable only over the LAN or Tailscale.

The crash-notifier on pve1 (192.168.50.101) sends Slack alerts via webhook on kernel panics. On 2026-04-25, Tom generalized the script to support pve2 and pve3 by parameterizing the $NODE variable. The new version is in homelab-playbook/scripts/crash-notifier.sh and is deployed via the homelab-infra ansible role to all three Proxmox nodes.
